<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="CalendulaAsteraceae" /></noinclude><section begin=par53 />{{GHGpar-heading|53|Hiphʿîl and Hophʿal}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|a}}
'''1.''' The characteristic of the active ({{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}) is a prefixed {{GHGheb|text=הַ}} (on its origin see {{GHGpar|55|i}}) in the perfect {{GHGheb|text=הִ}} (with the ''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ'', as in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}), which forms a closed syllable with the first consonant of the stem. The second syllable of the perfect had also originally an ''ă''; cf. the Arabic conj. iv. ''’aqtălă'', and in Hebrew the return of the {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the 2nd and 1st pers. {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטַ֫לְתָּ}}, &c. After the attenuation of this ''ă'' to ''ĭ'', it ought by rule to have been lengthened to ''ē'' in the tone-syllable, as in Aramaic {{GHGheb|text=אַקְטֵל}}, beside {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִל}} in Biblical Aramaic. Instead of this, however, it is always replaced in the strong verb by ''î'',<ref>This ''î'' may have been transferred originally from the imperfects of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, as a convenient means of distinction between the indicative and jussive, to the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of the strong verb and afterwards to the whole of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}; so Stade, Philippi, Praetorius, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1883, p. 52 f.</ref>{{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, but sometimes written defectively {{GHGheb|text=־ִ}}; cf. {{GHGpar|9|g}}. Similarly in the infinitive construct {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִיל}}, and in the imperfect and participle {{GHGheb|text=יַקְטִיל}} and {{GHGheb|text=טַקְטִיל}}, which are syncopated from {{GHGheb|text=יְהַקְטִיל}} and {{GHGheb|text=מְהַקְטִיל}}; {{GHGpar|23|k}}. The corresponding Arabic forms (''juqtĭl'' and ''muqtĭl'') point to an original ''ĭ'' in the second syllable of these forms. In Hebrew the regular lengthening of this ''ĭ'' to ''ē'' appears in the strong verb at least in the {{GHGterm|jussive}} and in the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} (see n), as also in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} of the 2nd sing. masc. (see m); on {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטֵ֫לְנָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּקְטֵ֫לְנָה}} cf. {{GHGpar|26|p}}. On the return of the original ''ă'' in the second syllable of the ''Imperat., Jussive'', &c, under the influence of a guttural, cf. {{GHGpar|65|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|b}}
In the {{GHGterm|passive}} ({{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}) the preformative is pronounced with an obscure vowel, whilst the second syllable has ''ă'' (in pause ''ā''), as its characteristic, thus:—''Perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָקְטַל}} or {{GHGheb|text=הֻקְטַל}}, ''Imperf.'' {{GHGheb|text=יָקְטַל}} (syncopated from {{GHGheb|text=יְהָקְטַל}}) or {{GHGheb|text=יֻקְטַל}}, ''Part.'' {{GHGheb|text=מָקְטָל}} or {{GHGheb|text=מֻקְטָל}} (from {{GHGheb|text=מְהָקְטָל}}); but the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} has the form {{GHGheb|text=הָקְטֵל}}.

Thus the characteristics of both conjugations are the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} preformative in the ''perfect, imperative'', and {{GHGterm|infinitive}}; in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle Hiphʿîl}}, Pathaḥ under the preformatives, in the ''Hophʿal ŏ'' or ''ŭ''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|c}}
'''2.''' The ''meaning'' of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} is primarily, and even more frequently than in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} ({{GHGpar|52|g}}), ''causative'' of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא|translate=to go forth}}, Hiph. ''to bring forth, to lead forth, to draw forth''; {{GHGheb|text=קָדַשׁ|translate=to be holy}}, Hiph. ''to sanctify''. Under the ''causative'' is also included (as in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}) the ''declarative'' sense, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִצְדִּיק|translate=to pronounce just}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִרְשִׁיעַ|translate=to make one an evil doer}} (''to pronounce guilty''); cf. {{GHGheb|text=עקשׁ}}, in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=20}}, ''to represent as perverse''. If Qal has already a transitive meaning, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} then takes two accusatives (see {{GHGpar|117|cc}}). In some verbs, {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} occur side by side in the same sense, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָבַד|translate=periit}}, Piʿēl and Hiphʿîl, ''perdidit''; as a rule,<section end=par53 /><noinclude>
